question: Does the prototype of a later call change how an earlier long constant argument is materialised? Positive control root:00BA f_00BA_0002 (worker resG, after VEC-1): 'f_171C_1A9E(0x100L, 1, "winheaders"); n = read(fd, f_171C_1B84(h), 0x100);' pushes the long 0x100 as 'mov cx,100h; sub dx,dx' only when read() has no prototype (or an old-style one, or count declared int); with the <io.h>-style prototype 'int read(int, void far *, unsigned int)' it is 'mov ax,100h; cwd'. Same family as PROTO-1 (the declared parameter type of a constant argument decides register choice for a neighbouring value). A two-call micro test does not show it; the probe therefore compiles the whole module 00BA. Spelling the constant as 0x100, 0x100U, 0x100L or 0x100UL makes no difference.
